messages:
jia (runtime): FYI customer HollowBank wants p99=200ms at sustained 2k qps for chat completions. they asked for commit in next contract cycle. thoughts on realistic knobs we can offer?

mike-sales: wow 200ms at 2k is pretty tight. can we propose tiered targets? maybe p95=120ms / p99=350ms as tradeoff? will save them $$ and still sell.

amanda (product): Sales asked for a firm SLA to sign. we need engineering options to present — what are the levers and estimated unit-cost delta? also need risk matrix if we promise 200ms.

jia (runtime): short list of levers: microbatch size (1..8), kernel path selection (fused-attn vs fallback), KV warmup/prefix cache, quantization profile (int8 vs float16), routing to dedicated pool vs hosted.

sam (sre): can we get a quick profiling run with HollowBank's sample workload (avg seq=96, tail prompts with long context) to see tail behavior? I suspect KV eviction + cold KV leading to long tails.

jia (runtime): ran a quick local perf pass earlier today with their prompt set: results below (dev box A100 80GB, cont-batcher on):

```
config: microbatch=1 | kernel=fused | quant=fp16 | kv_prefetch=on
qps=2k (sim) -> p50=18ms p95=110ms p99=420ms p999=980ms

config: microbatch=4 | kernel=fused | quant=fp16 | kv_prefetch=on
qps=2k -> p50=22ms p95=150ms p99=620ms p999=1400ms

config: microbatch=1 | kernel=fallback | quant=int8 | kv_prefetch=on
qps=2k -> p50=20ms p95=130ms p99=480ms
```

jia (runtime): takeaways: microbatching increases throughput but pushes tails up; fused kernel helps p95 but p99 still driven by KV miss/eviction and occasional scheduling jitter. int8 helps cost but sometimes regresses p99 depending on token patterns.

mike-sales: can we provide a customer-facing options doc: (A) p95-focused fast lane with p99 carveout, (B) premium dedicated with warmed KV and reserved CPUs for routing -> true 200ms p99? need numbers to price both.

amanda (product): yes — also include fallback policy: if p99 breaches, route small % of traffic to slower but stable model or reduce max_tokens to protect sla. list tradeoffs.

sam (sre): operational mitigations: KV pre-warming during traffic ramp, proactive eviction thresholds (LRU tuned by prompt length), and hot-key pinning for top prefixes. also add a tail-sampling alert (sample 0.1% requests at p99) to drive regressions.

jia (runtime): suggested customer proposal bullets:
- Option 1 (Standard): p95=120ms, p99<=450ms, microbatch=4, hosted best-effort. lower cost.
- Option 2 (Premium): p95<=110ms, p99<=220ms, reserved dedicated pool, microbatch=1, fused kernel pinned, KV pinned/warmed, 99.9% uptime SLA, +20% price premium.
- Option 3 (Aggressive low-latency lab): p95<=90ms, p99<=200ms (experimental): requires int8 tuning, kernel engineering, and strict admission control. exploratory pricing.

mike-sales: good. can you add expected token-cost delta and ops runbook for premium? customer will ask.

jia (runtime): estimated cost delta rough numbers: premium ~+35% infra cost vs standard at target qps due to reserved capacity and keeping microbatch=1. aggressive lab uncertain; may be +50% until kernel/quantization validated. will draft runbook steps: KV warmup script, rolling restart with warm cache, realtime tail monitor, canary policy.

amanda (product): i'll draft doc to share with HollowBank. ask engineering to add one more data point: p99 with a short 15-min soak after KV prewarm. that usually shows real-world tail improvement.

sam (sre): I'll schedule a 15-min soak test tonight on staging with KV prewarm and capture flamegraphs + scheduler traces. tagging ci-bot to create perf run.

ci-bot: perf-run-2070012345 started -> job 7732, collecting p50/p95/p99/p999, flamegraphs enabled.

jia (runtime): thanks. after run we should decide whether we can meet 200ms p99 on premium without heroic OS changes. if not, offer contractual carveouts and automated fallback to keep user experience intact. :thumbsup:

mike-sales: perfect. target to get a customer-ready slide deck by EOD tomorrow. will schedule call with HollowBank for end of week.

amanda (product): great collaboration. Jia/Sam, mark any followups in the proposal doc and PR the runbook snippets.

jia (runtime): will do — posting raw perf artifacts in #eng-runtime-perf later.
